summary: Registers the secret-token URI scheme, intended to help identify authentication tokens. Marking a token with a recognizable prefix makes it easier for tools to spot accidentally exposed secrets, for example in code repositories.

eli5.summary: Putting a clear label on a secret password so that software can notice if it gets left somewhere public by accident.

questions: what is the secret-token uri scheme
how to identify leaked authentication tokens
how to prevent leaking tokens in code
can i use secret-token for csrf tokens
subtitle: A URI scheme prefix that makes it easy to spot leaked authentication tokens in code.

tldr.problem: Developers often accidentally commit authentication tokens and API keys to public code repositories, giving attackers access to services.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8959 registers the secret-token URI scheme, a standard prefix like secret-token:abc123 that tools can scan for and flag as sensitive.
tldr.outcome: Source code repositories and continuous integration systems can now warn developers when they commit anything matching this pattern, reducing accidental token leaks.

today: RFC 8959 is an informational RFC that has been adopted by major code hosting platforms. GitLab and other services now offer secret scanning that detects the secret-token pattern.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content:
Bearer tokens and API keys are widely used for authentication. A bearer token is a secret that any party possessing it can use, without needing to prove ownership of any private key material.

The problem: developers regularly commit these tokens to public source code repositories by mistake. Tools that scan repositories have no reliable way to identify an arbitrary token as secret, so they miss many leaks. The RFC proposes a standard format to make tokens recognizable.
sections.eli5: Passwords and access tokens get checked into public code by accident all the time. With no standard way to label them, it is hard for security tools to spot and warn about the leak.

sections.title: The Format
sections.content:
The secret-token URI scheme uses the format secret-token:TOKEN, where TOKEN is any sequence of allowed URI characters (letters, digits, hyphen, period, underscore, tilde, and percent-encoded bytes).

For example: secret-token:E92FB7EB-D882-47A4-A265-A0B6135DC842%20foo. When used as a bearer token in HTTP, it is placed in the Authorization header as Authorization: Bearer secret-token:.... The entire URI must be used exactly, case-sensitive, without modification.
sections.eli5: Every token formatted like secret-token:somesecrethere can be automatically recognized by scanning tools.

sections.title: How It Helps
sections.content:
Once a service issues tokens with the secret-token prefix, source code repositories and CI systems can be configured to reject commits containing the pattern. GitHub and GitLab already offer secret scanning that can detect well-known token formats.

The RFC emphasizes this scheme is for generated tokens (API keys, access tokens) intended to be long-lived and reusable, not for ephemeral tokens like CSRF tokens used temporarily within a single session.
sections.eli5: Tools can now check code for anything starting with secret-token and warn the developer before it gets committed publicly.
